newsitem.title: USA: Miami carnival returns after 1996 plane downing.
newsitem.headline: Miami carnival returns after 1996 plane downing.

text.p: Miami's carnival, reputed to be the largest Hispanic street festival in North America, returned Sunday after being cancelled last year when Cuba shot down two planes flown by Cuban exiles.

An estimated 850,000 people crowded along a two-mile stretch of Eighth Street -- from which the festival got its nickname, Calle Ocho -- in the heart of Little Havana for salsa, merengue and Latin American cuisine. Organisers said they had expected up to one million people to attend the 20th annual street party.

The festival, put on by the local Kiwanis Club, was cancelled last year as the Cuban-American community mourned the deaths of four members of the exile group Brothers to the Rescue, whose planes were shot down by Cuban MiG fighters Feb. 24, 1996 over the Florida Straits.

"We understand that life must go on, and our pilots, the ones that died, would have wanted to see a happy Miami," Brothers to the Rescue founder Jose Basulto told CBS affiliate WFOR-TV. "We don't expect Calle Ocho to be suspended forever."

Police reported little trouble at the event. Festival-goers were cleared from a stretch of Eighth Street when an abandoned suitcase was spotted. It was opened and contained nothing dangerous, authorities said.
At least two people were arrested when a fight broke out, police said.
